title: How Slavery Ended in Stages
question: Why did ending slavery take so many separate steps?
hook: No single law ended slavery; it was taken apart piece by piece.
idea: Slavery ended in stages: trades were banned, colonies freed, then whole regions and finally the world.

beats.prompt: In 1807 Britain makes the slave trade illegal across its empire. What happens to people already enslaved in its colonies?

choices.label: They stay enslaved until a later law in 1833
They are freed the same year
choices.feedback: It tempts because the ban sounds total, but it covered the trade, not people already enslaved.

choices.label: They are freed within a year by a court ruling
choices.feedback: It sounds plausible after the Somersett case, but that case concerned English law, not the colonies.

beats.explain: The 1807 law stopped the trade, but existing slaves in British colonies were not liberated until the Slavery Abolition Act 1833.

beats.prompt: Put these steps against slavery in order of date.
items: The Somersett case rules slavery did not exist in English law
Britain makes the slave trade illegal across its empire
The United States passes the 13th Amendment
Brazil outlaws slavery, the last in the Americas

beats.prompt: Match each country to what it is known for in ending slavery.
pairs: New Laws of 1542 abolishing slavery for indigenous people
Last country in the Americas to outlaw it, in 1888
Latest to abolish officially, by decree in 1981
beats.explain: Each country marks a different turning point, from the 1500s to 1981.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: In 1948 the UN declared slavery illegal.
Even then, the Arab world still had legal chattel slavery.
Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Dubai abolished it in 1962–1963.
So Mauritania's 1981 decree cannot have been the latest abolition.
beats.explain: Mauritania is the latest country to officially abolish slavery, so the 1981 decree came after those earlier steps.
